question: why do supervised detectors trained on one attack category rank the other category's attacker messages below non-malicious messages (AUROC < 0.5)?
threshold_policy: validation-selected maximum-F1 threshold, per model and seed

features.unit: current-step (last window position) raw feature values, official splits
features.auroc_definition: single-feature AUROC of attacker vs non-malicious messages within one attack category, over messages where the feature is valid; > 0.5 means attackers have larger values, < 0.5 smaller values
features.benign_shift_definition: single-feature AUROC separating non-malicious dosAttack from non-malicious dataReplay training messages; 0.5 means no benign distribution shift

pooled:dataReplay.protocol: pooled official-split models; threshold maximizes F1 on this category's validation records; test restricted to this category

pooled:dosAttack.protocol: pooled official-split models; threshold maximizes F1 on this category's validation records; test restricted to this category

pooledthreshold:dataReplay.protocol: pooled official-split models and their single pooled validation-F1 threshold; test restricted to this category

pooledthreshold:dosAttack.protocol: pooled official-split models and their single pooled validation-F1 threshold; test restricted to this category

loao:dataReplay->dosAttack.protocol: fit and threshold on the source category's official train and validation splits; test on the target category's official test split

loao:dosAttack->dataReplay.protocol: fit and threshold on the source category's official train and validation splits; test on the target category's official test split

levels.receive_time_sender_rcvTime: (sender_id, rcvTime) of the retained receive copy
levels.bare_source_id: sender identifier without the archive prefix
levels.trajectory_window_L10: SHA-256 of the L = 10 model-input window (11 features and validity masks)

loao_sender_disjoint.protocol: normalization, all detectors, checkpoints, and validation-F1 thresholds fit on the source side only; evaluated on the disjoint target side
loao_sender_disjoint.partition_rule: bare source_ids ordered by sha256(salt:source_id) within attacker-ever and never-attacker strata; the first half is the source side (source-archive train and validation), the second half the target side (target-archive test)

procedures.youden_j: threshold maximizing validation TPR - FPR (Youden's J)
procedures.far_1.0pct: conservative validation quantile: non-malicious alert rate <= 1%
procedures.far_5.0pct: conservative validation quantile: non-malicious alert rate <= 5%

sender_overlap.definition: seen-sender test messages: official test messages whose bare source_id occurs in the official training split of the same archive; unseen-sender: all other official test messages. Thresholds are the pooled validation-F1 thresholds.

label_granularity.definition: VeReMi NextGen assigns attacker labels at sender level during attack windows. message_corroborated: attacker records whose payload diverges from the official ground truth (dataReplay) or that have no ground-truth broadcast (dosAttack injected); sender_level_genuine_state: dosAttack attacker records whose payload equals the genuine sender state, which a detector can flag only through window context such as timing, not through payload falsification. AUROC compares each group with all non-malicious test records of the same context.

official.protocol: pooled official models on the full official test split with their pooled validation-F1 thresholds

loao:dataReplay->dosAttack.protocol: LOAO models with source-category validation-F1 thresholds

loao:dosAttack->dataReplay.protocol: LOAO models with source-category validation-F1 thresholds
